title: Edge-Coloring Power Graphs: the intersection power graph is Class 2 exactly for cyclic groups of odd prime-power order (Theorem 3.2)
author: Elie Feinsilber
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the theorem printed as Theorem 3.2 of "Edge-Coloring Power Graphs" (source0.tex lines 547--551, source label thm:intersection-power), delivered with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 553--592 (40 lines, one adjacent proof environment). It is one of the article's main results: it classifies the edge-chromatic number of the intersection power graph of a finite group, showing that G_I(G) is Class 2 exactly when G is cyclic of odd prime-power order, and it is proved by first reducing to groups of odd order, then treating cyclic p-groups, noncyclic p-groups and finally groups divisible by two distinct primes, where the solvability of odd-order groups (Feit-Thompson) and Hall's theorem produce coprime Hall subgroups whose mutual non-adjacency, together with an explicit edge count, shows the graph is not overfull and hence Class 1. The proof is complete inside the retained span. It is above ordinary PhD qualifying level: it combines the overfullness criterion for the chromatic index with structure theory of finite groups (unique subgroups of order p in cyclic p-groups, Hall subgroups, the Feit-Thompson theorem) to obtain a complete algebraic characterization of an NP-complete property on a family of graphs. Rated H2 because the argument, although it uses deep classification theorems, is a compact case analysis that the article presents as one of several parallel main theorems rather than as its deepest technical achievement.
